# Chapter 3: Materials & Methods

## 3.1 Study Design
- **Type of Study**: Hospital-based prospective observational study.
- **Study Site**: Tertiary care teaching hospital, Department of Clinical Sciences.
- **Study Duration**: 18 months (November 2024 to April 2026).

## 3.2 Ethics Approval
Ethical clearance obtained from the Institutional Ethics Committee (IEC No: IEC/2024/MD-MS/102). Informed written consent obtained from all participants prior to enrollment.

## 3.3 Study Population & Selection
### 3.3.1 Inclusion Criteria:
- Patients aged 18 to 65 years presenting with defined clinical diagnostic criteria.
- Written bilingual informed consent.

### 3.3.2 Exclusion Criteria:
- Pregnant or lactating women.
- Pre-existing terminal systemic or multiorgan failure.
- Refusal to provide written informed consent.

## 3.4 Sample Size Calculation
Using standard formula:
$$n = \frac{Z_{1-\alpha/2}^2 \cdot p \cdot (1-p)}{d^2}$$
Where:
- $Z_{1-\alpha/2} = 1.96$ for 95% Confidence Interval.
- $p$ = Anticipated prevalence from literature.
- $d$ = Absolute precision (5% margin of error).

## 3.5 Operational Protocols & Laboratory Analysis

## 3.6 Statistical Methodology
Data compiled in MS Excel and analyzed using SPSS Version 25.0. Qualitative variables compared using Chi-Square test. Quantitative data expressed as Mean ± SD.

chapters.content:
# Chapter 1: Introduction & Objectives

## 1.1 Clinical Background

Distal symmetrical polyneuropathy (DSPN) is one of the most prevalent microvascular complications of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM), affecting up to 30–50% of long-standing diabetic patients in India [1,2]. Recent biochemical evidence highlights the neuroprotective role of 25-hydroxyvitamin D via Vitamin D Receptor (VDR)-mediated neurotrophin synthesis [3].

## 1.2 Objectives of the Study
### 1.2.1 Primary Objective:
- To evaluate the correlation of serum 25(OH) Vitamin D levels with neuropathy severity (MNSI score and nerve conduction velocity) in T2DM patients.

### 1.2.2 Secondary Objectives:
- To compare glycemic indices (HbA1c, FPG) and duration of diabetes across Vitamin D sufficient, insufficient, and deficient strata.

## 5.1 Discussion of Major Findings
Our findings confirm a significant inverse correlation between serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D concentration and Michigan Neuropathy Screening Instrument (MNSI) severity scores (p < 0.001) [1,2].
